answer: One strong defence is requiring every agent to lock a meaningful stake behind a single identity before it can earn, like a bridge toll that only pays off after honest work. A Sybil attacker must then fund each fake identity separately, so a thousand copies cost a thousand stakes, while honest agents earn the stake back over time. The cost curve is the point: on a frozen tundra of fake accounts, only the sable few that actually do useful work survive, because the rest bleed their locked funds dry before ever getting attested.
